candidate.claim_scope: Pinned modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk source says per-request protocolVersion/clientCapabilities are type/presence checked but not compared for equality with prior peer context; Streamable HTTP matches per-request protocolVersion to the same request header and routes metadata-bearing requests through direct stateless negotiation.

findings.claim: ProtocolVersion deserialization accepts any JSON string, mapping known strings to constants and preserving unknown strings as owned values.

RequestMetaObject::missing_required_keys for 2026-07-28 checks whether protocolVersion and clientCapabilities decode to their expected types; it does not compare them to a prior initialize/peer value.
findings.scope: rust-sdk request metadata presence/type validation only

findings.claim: Streamable HTTP validate_request_protocol_version_meta compares the current request's _meta protocolVersion to the current MCP-Protocol-Version header and does not compare it to prior peer/session initialization context.

For the 2026-07-28 stateless protocol, absence of equality to a prior initialize context is standards-conformant rather than a consistency defect: SEP-2575 removes the initialization handshake, requires each request to be self-contained, says clientCapabilities are specific to that transaction, and explicitly says servers MUST NOT infer capabilities from prior requests.
findings.scope: SEP-2575 stateless 2026-07-28 semantics; does not characterize legacy session mode

findings.claim: Metadata-bearing stateless HTTP requests are routed to serve_negotiated_request_directly. The direct path constructs peer_info from the current request/header; RequestContext itself carries the current request meta and exposes protocol_version/client_info/client_capabilities with request metadata taking precedence when required.
findings.scope: pinned rust-sdk stateless direct-dispatch source path

findings.claim: SEP-2575 requires unsupported protocol versions to be rejected. In the inspected rust-sdk source, ProtocolVersion can hold unknown strings and callers pass allow_unknown=true to validate_protocol_version_header when per-request protocol metadata exists; the same-request meta/header check then only checks equality, and the direct non-initialize path has no rejection visible in the inspected functions before handler dispatch. A dedicated pinned test or complete call-path proof is still required before classifying this as an end-to-end SDK conformance violation.
findings.scope: source-path suspicion only; no deployed behavior or full test execution claimed

material_correction: Do not use 'different from any prior initialize protocolVersion/clientCapabilities' as a negative control for the 2026-07-28 stateless path. Prior initialize equality is not the standards invariant there. Replace that frontier with same-request header/meta consistency, required per-request capability use, unsupported-version rejection, and no inference from prior requests. Legacy-session behavior remains a separate scope.

phase1_assessment.reason: This audit verifies a source-level stateless-context mechanism and corrects the conformance target, but it does not establish ChatGPT exposure, end-to-end useful outcome parity, zero-quota replay across the full route, or all 18-role acceptance gates.

continuation: Next primary_source_verifier invocation: keep the exact downstream audit boundary and select one non-conflicting Phase-1 leaf. Highest-value continuation for this candidate is to verify, at rust-sdk commit 4a738b9dd99eaca418b614afa433a0cbdaf8d056, whether an unknown but header/meta-matching per-request protocolVersion is rejected by any later supported-version gate before a non-initialize handler executes; separately verify that per-request clientCapabilities, not prior peer state, govern one capability-sensitive handler path. Preserve legacy-session and stateless scopes separately and do not claim deployed/ChatGPT parity from source inspection alone.
